title: Tobacco
preamble: Sixteen answers need to undergo a “metallic” change before entry. In the remaining clues the wordplay indicates the answer with an extra letter that is not entered in the grid; these letters, in clue order, should make all clear. Chambers Dictionary (2003) is the primary reference.

clue.text: Twice hinder Scotty running round a notorious shoreline? (two words)

indicators.note: going round something means wrapping it on both sides
letters that are running about are loose and free to change order
a word said twice means its letters are set down two times in a row

parts.note: to bar is to block or obstruct
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written, held inside the rearranged name

explanation.surface: Someone tells a dog called Scotty, twice over, to stop running around some infamous stretch of coast.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the unaltered clues, so the wordplay yields one letter too many: a spare T, which is not entered and starts the hidden message.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barbary Coast of North Africa was notorious for centuries as the base of corsairs and slave raiders.

clue.text: Row and work ship

parts.note: to row is to pull an oar, and an oar is the thing you row with
a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: A sailor's instruction: pull on the oars and get the vessel going.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay spells one letter more than the grid takes; the leading O is the spare letter that joins the message.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo is the ship of Greek legend in which Jason and the Argonauts sailed for the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Horse close to endless spiders

indicators.note: with no end, a word loses its final letter

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse
close to means near

explanation.surface: A horse grazes in a corner that is crawling with spiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' acts only on the word for close. The horse's B is the extra letter the grid does not take.
explanation.definitionFit: Aranea is the Latin name for the spider genus, used in Chambers as a collective name for spiders.

clue.text: Introduced first class Titian works by Edward

indicators.note: works here is a verb of making: the letters are worked into new shapes

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I
the painter's name, taken as written
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone launched a range of top-quality Titian paintings alongside works by an Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun for paintings but is the rearranging verb. One A from the shuffled letters is spare and goes to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to introduce or begin it, and an initiated person has been introduced into a group.

clue.text: Face recognised in Icelandic album

indicators.note: something recognised in a phrase is spotted among its letters, so only a stretch of them is kept

parts.note: the closing three letters of the word
the opening two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A familiar face spotted on the cover of a record from Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters run straight across the word break, as in a hidden word, but there are five of them; the C is the extra letter for the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Dial is slang for a person's face, and a clock face is also called its dial.

clue.text: Aliens ravished moonstruck girl?

indicators.note: something ravished has been violently disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl dazzled by the moon is carried off by space invaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SELINA, but this is one of the sixteen metallic entries: the S and N (Sn, the symbol for tin) come out and T goes in, so the grid gets TELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Selina is a girl's name related to Selene, the Greek moon goddess, so its bearer is playfully linked with the moon.

clue.text: Former fuss about forbidden plant of the clover genus

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, enclosing it

parts.note: coil is an old word for tumult or bother, as in Hamlet's mortal coil
tref describes food forbidden under Jewish dietary law, the opposite of kosher

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned row over a banned clover-like plant.
explanation.walkthrough: With the outer word wrapped round the inner, the result starts with a C that is not entered; it is this clue's message letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is a name for clover and its relatives in the genus Trifolium, plants with three-lobed leaves.

clue.text: Look into hospital room

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside the other word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SALON; as a metallic entry it loses its S and N and gains a T, so ALTO goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a large reception room or drawing room in a grand house.

clue.text: Nutritive cereal starts to upset Ian's Nigerian monkey

parts.note: sago is a starchy food from palm pith, often counted among cereals

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, one taken from each

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: A Nigerian monkey is put off its food by a nourishing grain dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SAGOUIN; as a metallic entry its S and N come out and a T goes in, giving AGOUTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The sagouin is a small South American monkey, a marmoset; Nigerian only colours the surface.

clue.text: Fate encountered by oiks in revolt

indicators.note: rebels in revolt overturn the existing order, as these letters are

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged; an oik is British slang for a lout
to have encountered someone is to have met them

explanation.surface: A grim fate meets a gang of rebellious louts.
explanation.walkthrough: An oik is British slang for an uncouth lout. The rearranged letters have an O to spare, which goes to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a Turkish borrowing from Arabic meaning destiny or fate.

clue.text: Critically examines container aboard ship

indicators.note: cargo aboard a vessel is carried within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a shipping container on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SCANS; as a metallic entry it loses its S and N and gains a T, so CATS goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a text or picture is to scrutinise it closely, looking it over with care.

clue.text: Unusual laic type of copy

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters leave their usual order

parts.note: both words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A layman of an odd sort turns out to be a kind of copy.
explanation.walkthrough: Laic means lay, not clerical. The rearranged letters leave one I over, the message letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectypal is the adjective from ectype, a reproduction or copy, as opposed to the original or prototype.

clue.text: What are spun from vascular bundles

parts.note: a stele is the central vascular cylinder of a plant stem; one plural is stelae

explanation.surface: A botany question: what fibres can be spun from a plant's vascular tissue?
explanation.walkthrough: The opening S of the botanical plural is the spare letter for the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Tela is Latin for a web, so telae are webs, the things spiders spin.

clue.text: Follows headless bird

indicators.note: without a head, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: to trail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: Someone tracks a bird that has had its head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' seems to describe the bird but acts on the verb. After the head goes, the final S is spare and joins the message.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a marsh bird of the family that includes the corncrake and the water rail.

clue.text: Foolishly midshipman pinches his frisky girl's bottom

indicators.note: to pinch something is to squeeze it between two sides
frisky means playful and lively, so the letters jump about

parts.note: snotty is old naval slang for a midshipman
rearranged

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: A naval cadet misbehaves by pinching a playful girl's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' reads as groping but is the containment signal. The naval slang word supplies an N that is not entered: that is the message letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sottish means stupid or drunken like a sot, so sottishly means foolishly.

clue.text: Actor's also into American margarine

indicators.note: going into something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: oleo is a US word for margarine
too means also

explanation.surface: An actor is also into margarine from America, perhaps advertising it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the possessive name, read as 'the actor's'. The spread's last letter, an O, is not entered and goes to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter O'Toole was the Irish-born actor famed for Lawrence of Arabia, so the clue's possessive points at his surname.

clue.text: Note one seabird

parts.note: soh or sol is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
an means one

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher jots down a single seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SOLAN; as a metallic entry it loses S and N and gains T, so TOLA is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: The solan or solan goose is an old name for the gannet, a large diving seabird.

clue.text: Alison's mad with college of lunar studies

indicators.note: mad means deranged, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: the name, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Alison has gone crazy over a college devoted to the study of the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alison’s' is read as 'Alison is'. The clue gives SELENOLOGICAL; as a metallic entry its S and N come out and a T goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Selenology is the scientific study of the moon, from Greek selene, so selenological relates to lunar science.

clue.text: Substrate cut in region of synclinal structure

indicators.note: a cut word has been trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: a substrate is an underlying base layer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geologist's note about a layer sliced through in a folded rock area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but supplies letters. The clue gives BASIN; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology a basin is an area where strata dip inward towards a centre, a synclinal structure.

clue.text: Battle to secure border after a chase?

indicators.note: coming after puts this piece behind what precedes it

parts.note: taken as written
to run something down is to chase it; a run is a pursuit
a hem is a border secured by folding and stitching

explanation.surface: A military plan: after a pursuit, fight to hold the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The U from the pursuit word is the spare letter the grid does not take.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnhem was the 1944 battle in the Netherlands where Allied airborne troops failed to hold the Rhine bridge.

clue.text: Master takes aboard last of Indian warrant officers

indicators.note: to take something aboard is to carry it inside

parts.note: a boss is a master or employer

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A ship's master takes on the last of the Indian petty officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives BOS'NS, a contracted plural of boatswains; as a metallic entry the S and N go and T comes in, giving BOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain or bos'n is a ship's officer in charge of rigging and boats, traditionally a warrant officer.

clue.text: Tina's age is disposed to fatten

indicators.note: things disposed are laid out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Tina has reached the age where she is inclined to put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed' looks like 'inclined' but is the rearranging signal. The clue gives SAGINATE; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Saginate is a rare verb from Latin saginare, meaning to feed up or fatten livestock.

clue.text: French tenor gets to the heart of Venice

parts.note: Antoine Trial was an 18th-century French tenor, and a light comic tenor voice is still called a trial after him
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French opera singer finally reaches the centre of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets to the heart of' reads as one phrase, but 'gets' is the link and 'to' supplies letters. The singer's opening T is spare and goes to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the old commercial district of Venice around the famous bridge over the Grand Canal, the city's historic centre.

clue.text: Loose rock at noon to shelter …

parts.note: scree is loose broken rock on a slope
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Climbers on loose rock at midday look for cover, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SCREEN; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in, giving CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to shield or protect it from view or danger.

clue.text: … any Sioux wandering around Alabama uneasily

indicators.note: going around something encloses it
wandering things stray from their path, so the letters move around

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: some Sioux roam nervously around Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the clue before but plays no part in the wordplay. One A is spare and joins the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiously means in a worried, uneasy way, so the two adverbs are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Liquids flowed under middle of Naseby

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so coming after
the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of the place name
a liquid that flowed ran

explanation.surface: Liquids, perhaps blood, flowed beneath the middle of the Civil War battlefield of Naseby.
explanation.walkthrough: Naseby, a Northamptonshire village, was the 1645 English Civil War battle. The final N of the verb for flowed is the spare message letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sera is the plural of serum, the clear watery fluid of blood, so they are liquids.

clue.text: Crooked time-wasting Latins are fond of being sluggish

indicators.note: wasting time here means losing the letter that stands for time
something crooked is bent out of its straight order

parts.note: the word with its T for time taken out
to be fond of things is to like them

explanation.surface: Dishonest Latins who waste time are happy to be slow.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time. The clue gives SNAIL-LIKE; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in, giving TAILLIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is the proverbial slow mover, so snail-like means sluggish.

clue.text: Girl gets new resin

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A girl buys some fresh resin.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SARAN; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in, giving TARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Saran is a trade name for a polymer resin of vinylidene chloride, used in plastic films.

clue.text: Ed's found a home for and I sold something used in castings

parts.note: plast is Edmund Spenser's past tense of place, to find a home for
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ed rehomed an item and I sold something used in metal casting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed is Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet whose archaic forms Chambers lists. The final D of the selling word is the spare message letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastisol is PVC suspended in a plasticiser, poured into moulds and heated to make castings.

clue.text: Karen plastered in black deposit — a reputed cure for bites

indicators.note: one piece goes in, inside the other

parts.note: soot is the black deposit left by smoke

indicators.note: plastered is slang for very drunk, and drunk letters stagger out of order

parts.note: the name, taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Drunk Karen is daubed in soot, and someone suggests a folk remedy for bites.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SNAKEROOT; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in, so TAKEROOT is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakeroot names several plants whose roots were once believed to cure venomous snakebite.

clue.text: Silencers, containing shredded lint, for a type of gun

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside

parts.note: gags silence people

indicators.note: shredded material is torn apart, so its letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Silencers packed with shredded lint, made to fit a particular gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silencers' suggests gun mufflers, but these are gags. Their final S is the spare letter that goes to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gatling gun is an early hand-cranked machine gun named after its inventor Richard Gatling.

clue.text: Shame for offence in the army! Just the reverse

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
this phrase swaps which piece holds and which is held, undoing what the words before it say

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A soldier is disgraced for an offence in the army, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' tells the solver to put the army in the offence, not the offence in the army. The clue gives STAIN; as a metallic entry the S and N go and T comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on someone's character is a mark of disgrace or shame.

clue.text: Against introducing repulsive old goddess

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it inside

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
loth in an obsolete sense meant hateful or repulsive

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to bringing in a hideous ancient deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The final N of the word for against is the spare message letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, the goddess who spins the thread of life.

clue.text: Stew limpets

parts.note: Patella is the genus of limpets

explanation.walkthrough: The T in the middle of the genus name is the spare letter that goes to the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish cooked with seafood and meat, loosely called a stew.

clue.text: Arrangement for Polonia after striking new coin

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters into a different order
after striking something out, that letter is gone

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A plan for Poland, drawn up after a new coin is minted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests minting a coin but means crossing out. One I in the rearranged letters is spare and joins the message.
explanation.definitionFit: A paolo was an old silver coin of the Papal States, named after Pope Paul III.

clue.text: Jack left Bishop of Ypres in Dutch community

indicators.note: a letter that has left is no longer present

parts.note: Cornelius Jansen, founder of Jansenism, was Bishop of Ypres
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards; it is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A sailor walked out on a Flemish bishop who lived among the Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives ANSEN; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in, so ANTE is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ansen is a village in the Drenthe province of the Netherlands, so a small Dutch community.

clue.text: Antelope is back in health farm

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, a place for recovering health

indicators.note: going back means running the letters the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An antelope has returned to the spa.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives SASIN; as a metallic entry its S and N go and T comes in, so ASTI is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: The sasin is the Indian blackbuck, a species of antelope.

clue.text: Bovine girl is touring New York

indicators.note: touring a place means going all round it

parts.note: gal is a casual word for a girl
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A cow-like girl goes on a tour of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bovine' reads as an insult about the girl but is the definition, a noun here. The N of the city's abbreviation is the spare message letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The gyal or gayal is a domesticated ox of South and Southeast Asia, so a bovine animal.
